source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And as Yeshua looked up, he saw them — those who were depositing their gifts [or: offerings] into the collection chest — and they were wealthy [or: prosperous]

translation_notes: ראה (ר-א-ה): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh (name)'. Chose H7200 because the context requires a finite verb — Yeshua performed the action of seeing.
והם (ה-ם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. Chose H1992 because the sentence requires a pronoun subject for the predicate 'rich.'
textual_notes: בתיבה — 'chest/box' from תיבה (as in Noah's ark/container). No Strong's candidates were provided; the word clearly means a collection container in this context.
שמשימין — a participial form with ש- (that/who) prefix + משימין (placing), typical of later Hebrew/Aramaic construction. No Strong's candidates provided.

verses.literal: And looking Yeshua saw them that were placing their gifts in the chest and they [were] rich

verses.translation: And he saw a certain poor [or: destitute] woman who put in two small coins [perutot] of small [or: diminished] value

translation_notes: שני (ש-נ-י): Candidates: H8144 'crimson/scarlet', H8145 'second/double/two', H5204 'lamentation'. Chose H8145 because the context describes a quantity of coins — 'two small coins' fits the narrative of a poor woman's offering.

מערך (מ-ע-ר-ך): Candidates: H4633 'arrangement/mental disposition', H6186 'to arrange/set in order', H6187 'a pile/equipment/estimate (value)'. Chose H6187 because the phrase describes the monetary worth of the coins — 'of small value/estimate.'
קטן (ק-ט-ן): Candidates: H6994 'to diminish', H6995 'little finger', H6996 'diminutive/small', H6997 'Katan (name)'. Chose H6996 because it modifies מערך as an adjective — 'small value.'

ששמה: The ש prefix = 'that/who', and שמה here functions as 'she placed/put.' The Strong's candidates H8047 'ruin' and H8048 'Shammah (name)' do not fit; this is a verbal form שם (to put/place, H7760) with feminine suffix and relative prefix.
textual_notes: א)ה — likely אשה (woman), with the shin partially damaged or marked with a special character. No Strong's candidates provided.
פשיטין — an Aramaic loanword for small coins (perutot/peshitin). No Strong's candidates provided.
ששמה — parsed as ש + שמה (that she placed). The Strong's entries for שמה (H8047 'ruin', H8048 'Shammah') are noun/proper noun readings that do not fit this verbal context.

verses.literal: And he saw a woman one poor that placed two small coins of value small

verses.translation: And he said: In truth I say to you that this poor [or: afflicted] widow placed [in] more than all of you — praises [upon] praises [or: psalms of praise]

translation_notes: ואמר (א-מ-ר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H562 'something said (Aramaic)', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because the context requires a finite verb of speech — 'and he said.'

שמה: Same as section 2 — this is ש + שמה (that she placed, from שם H7760). The Strong's candidates H8047 'ruin' and H8048 'Shammah' do not fit the verbal context where the widow is the subject performing an action.

אומר: The only Strong's candidate is H201 'Omar (name)'. However, the consonants א-ו-מ-ר are clearly a participle of אמר 'to say' — 'I [am] saying to you.' This is a standard participial form of H559.
textual_notes: תהלים תהלות — This doubling is unusual. תהלים could be 'psalms' or 'praises' (from תהלה, H8416). תהלות is the feminine plural of the same root. The doubling may be an intensifying construction meaning 'abundant praises' or it could be a scribal notation. The phrase may modify what preceded — that her small gift constitutes greater praise than all others.
בא6מת — the numeral marker 6 in the middle suggests a scribal notation or damaged text. Reading as באמת 'in truth.'
א$ני — reading as אני 'I', with the $ marking some textual feature.

verses.literal: And he said in truth saying to you I that this the widow the poor placed more than all of you praises praises

verses.translation: For all these [people] gave from their overflow [or: abundance], placing [it] as a gift to God, but this [woman] gave from what she lacked — and there is to her a deficiency — she placed all her sustenance [or: food] that she had

translation_notes: אלו (consonants אלו): Candidates: H431 'lo!/these', H432 'if'. Chose H431 because the context describes a group ('all these') who gave from abundance, functioning as a demonstrative pronoun.

במתן (consonants מתן): Candidates: H4975 'loins', H4976 'a present/gift', H4977 'Mattan (name)', H8565 'monster'. Chose H4976 because the context is about giving offerings — 'in the gift of God' fits perfectly.
האל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because with the definite article ה, 'the God' makes sense as the recipient of the gift.

אבל (consonants אבל): Candidates: H56 'to bewail', H57 'lamenting', H58 'meadow', H61 'but/truly'. Chose H61 because it serves as an adversative conjunction contrasting the wealthy givers with this woman.

שמה: This word is ambiguous — candidates include H8047 'ruin/desolation' and a form of שים 'to place/put'. In context, 'she placed all her food' is coherent, reading שמה as a 3fs perfect of שים (to place). The reading 'ruin' would be incoherent here.
שהיה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because 'that was to her' = 'that she had' is the natural relative clause.
textual_notes: מהשפעתם has no Strong's candidates listed — it appears to be a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'from their abundance/overflow' (from root שפע).
!פיחתה is marked with ! indicating textual uncertainty — it appears to derive from a root meaning 'to diminish/lack' (פחת), reading 'what she lacked'.
שמה could be parsed as H8047 'desolation' or as a 3fs form of שים 'to place'. Context strongly favors 'she placed'.

verses.literal: For all these from their abundance placed [it] in [the] gift of God but this [one] from what she lacked and there is to her deficiency she placed all her food that was to her

verses.translation: And some [of them] were saying that the Temple [or: sanctuary] which had been adorned with precious stones [or: stones of pearls] and with gifts — and Yeshua said

translation_notes: שהיה (consonants היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be', H1962 'ruin', H3050 'Yah'. Chose H1961 because 'that was adorned' describes the state of the Temple.
אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the verb 'said' naturally follows the subject 'Yeshua'.
textual_notes: מעוטר has no Strong's candidates — appears to be a passive participle of עטר 'to crown/adorn'.
מרגליות has no Strong's candidates — this is a post-biblical Hebrew term for pearls or precious stones.
וממתנות appears related to מתנה (gift/present) — with prefix ומ and plural construct, 'and from gifts'.

verses.literal: And some [were] saying that the sanctuary that was adorned from stones of pearls and from gifts and Yeshua said

verses.translation: These things that you are seeing — yet [or: still] you will see days when not [a single] stone will stand upon [another] stone and [it] will be destroyed [or: ruined]

translation_notes: אלו (consonants אלו): Candidates: H431 'lo!/these', H432 'if'. Chose H431 as a demonstrative 'these' modifying 'things'.
אבן (consonants אבן): Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 'a stone', H70 'pair of stones/potter's wheel'. Chose H68 because individual stones of a building are in view.
על (consonants על): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/over', H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 because 'stone upon stone' is the natural spatial image of stacked masonry.
textual_notes: ותפסד has no Strong's candidates — appears to be from root פסד meaning 'to be ruined/destroyed', a post-biblical Hebrew form.
עדיין has no Strong's candidates — a post-biblical Hebrew adverb meaning 'still/yet'.
שאתם: The only Strong's candidate given is H864 'Etham', which is a place name. Here it clearly functions as the relative particle ש + pronoun אתם 'you' (2mp).

verses.literal: Things these that you [are] seeing still you will see days that not will stand stone upon stone and [it] will be ruined

verses.translation: And they asked him Master [or: Lord] when will all these things come to pass and when will they begin to be accomplished [or: to happen]

translation_notes: אדון (consonants אדון): Candidates: H113 'sovereign/controller', H114 'Addon (name)'. Chose H113 because 'Master/Lord' is the address to Yeshua, coherent with the question being directed to him.

אלה (consonants אלה): Multiple candidates including H421 'bewail', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H426 'God'. Here אלה functions as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (standard Hebrew אלה), modifying 'the things'. None of the Strong's candidates perfectly match the demonstrative, but in context this is clearly the demonstrative pronoun.
להעשות: Strong's candidates H6219 'polished' and H6220 'Ashvath' don't fit. This is the nif'al/hitpa'el infinitive of עשה (H6213 'to do/make') — 'to be done/accomplished'.
textual_notes: אלה as demonstrative 'these' is not well-represented in the Strong's candidates provided (which list verbal and nominal forms). The demonstrative pronoun אלה is typically H428.
להעשות — the Strong's candidates given (H6219, H6220) don't match; this is clearly an infinitive construct of עשה 'to do/make' in a passive/reflexive stem.

verses.literal: And they asked him Master when will be all these the things and when will they begin to be done

verses.translation: And he said Guard [or: Watch] yourselves so that no man will deceive [or: defraud] you for many will come in my name who will say to you I — I am he and the time [or: the appointed season] draws near — and then you shall not desire [or: choose] to go after them

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 — verb 'said' naturally follows 'and he'.

אי זה (consonants אי + זה): For אי: H335 'where', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. For זה: H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Together אי זה functions as an indefinite pronoun 'any/whichever' in post-biblical Hebrew, meaning 'any' man.
איש (consonants איש): Candidates: H376 'a man', H377 'to be manly'. Chose H376 because 'man' completes the phrase 'any man'.

יונה (consonants יונה): Candidates: H3123 'a dove', H3124 'Jonah'. Neither fits as a verb here. However, in post-biblical Hebrew, the root ינה means 'to deceive/defraud/oppress'. Reading יונה as a 3ms imperfect of ינה 'to deceive' produces the coherent warning 'no man will deceive you'. A 'dove' or 'Jonah' inserted here produces nonsense.
הוא (consonants הוא): Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 — 'I am he' is the claim of the false messiahs.
בשמי: Strong's candidates given are H8060 'Shammai' and H4310 'who'. Neither fits. This is clearly ב + שם + י = 'in my name', with שם (H8034 'name') plus 1cs possessive suffix.
textual_notes: ה!מרו is marked with ! indicating textual uncertainty. It could be from שמר 'to guard/watch' (הִשָּׁמְרוּ) or from אמר 'to say'. Context strongly favors שמר — 'guard yourselves' is a standard warning formula.

יונה as a verb 'to deceive' from root ינה is not reflected in the Strong's candidates provided (which only list 'dove' and 'Jonah'). The post-biblical verbal sense 'to deceive/wrong' fits the context perfectly.
בשמי: The Strong's candidates do not include שם H8034 'name'; reading as 'in my name' (ב+שם+י) is contextually certain.

verses.literal: And he said be guarded to yourselves that any man not will deceive you for many will come in my name that will say to you that I I [am] he and the time draws near and then you not will desire to go after them

verses.translation: And when you hear disputes [or: quarrels] and groanings [or: sighing] do not be terrified [or: tremble] for all these things are destined [or: obligated] to happen — surely [or: indeed] this will not be immediately nor [will it be] the end

translation_notes: וכאשר (consonants אשר): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר = 'when/as' is the standard temporal conjunction.

אל (consonants אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 because אל + imperfect verb תחרדו = 'do not tremble', a standard prohibitive construction.
זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this'. Chose H2088 — 'this will not be immediately' is coherent.
מיד (consonants יד): Candidate H3027 'hand'. Here מיד functions adverbially as 'immediately/at once' (literally 'from hand'), a well-known Hebrew idiom.
אלה: As in section 4, this is the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428), though the provided candidates don't include the demonstrative form.
textual_notes: קטטות has no Strong's candidates — appears to be plural of קטטה 'quarrel/strife', from root קטט.
ואנחות has no Strong's candidates — plural of אנחה 'groaning/sighing' (related to H585 אנחה).
שחוייב has no Strong's candidates — appears to be a post-biblical passive participle from root חיב 'to be obligated/liable'.
תחרדו has no Strong's candidates — imperfect 2mp of חרד 'to tremble/be terrified' (related to H2729).

verses.literal: And when you will hear quarrels and groanings do not tremble that [it is] obligated all these to be done surely not will be this immediately and not the end

verses.translation: Then he said to them Peoples [or: nations] will rise against peoples and kingdom against kingdom

translation_notes: אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb'. Chose H559 — 'he said to them' is the natural narrative verb.

להם (consonants הם): Candidates: H3859 'to burn/rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Here להם is the preposition ל + 3mp pronoun 'to them'. H1992 'they' is the pronoun base; with ל prefix it means 'to them'.

נגד (consonants נגד): Candidates: H5046 'to front/declare', H5047 'to flow', H5048 'opposite/against', H5049 'opposite'. Chose H5048 because 'against' fits the adversarial context of nations rising against nations.
מלכות (second instance): Candidates: H4438 'a rule/dominion', H3575 'Cuth'. Chose H4438 — 'kingdom against kingdom' parallels 'peoples against peoples'.

verses.literal: Then he said to them will rise peoples against peoples and kingdom against kingdom

verses.translation: And [a] great earthquake [or: shaking] will be in [various] places and plagues and famine and terrors [or: fearful events] and great signs in the heavens [or: skies]

translation_notes: ורעש (consonants רעש): Candidates: H7493 'to undulate/shake', H7494 'vibration/bounding/uproar'. Chose H7494 (noun) because 'a great earthquake' is the subject of 'will be'.
ורעב (consonants רעב): Candidates: H7456 'to hunger', H7457 'hungry', H7458 'hunger/famine'. Chose H7458 (noun) because it appears in a list of nouns (plagues, famine, terrors).
textual_notes: ב!מים is marked with ! indicating textual uncertainty. The most likely reading is בשמים 'in the heavens/skies' (from שמים H8064), with the ש possibly damaged or missing in the manuscript. Alternatively it could be במים 'in the waters' but the context of cosmic signs favors 'in the skies'.
ומגפות has no Strong's candidates — plural of מגפה 'plague/pestilence' (related to H4046).
וחרדות has no Strong's candidates — plural of חרדה 'trembling/terror' (related to H2731).
ואותות has no Strong's candidates — plural of אות 'sign' (related to H226).

verses.literal: And earthquake great will be in places and plagues and famine and terrors and signs great in the skies

verses.translation: But [or: only] before all these things they will lay their hands on you and persecute you and deliver you up to houses of assembly [or: synagogues] and to their prisons to hand you over to great kings for the sake of my name

translation_notes: רק (consonants רק): Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'but/only before all these things' introduces a temporal qualification — a natural adverbial use.
אלה: As before, functioning as demonstrative pronoun 'these'.

למסור (consonants סור): Candidates: H5493 'to turn off', H5494 'deteriorated', H5495 'Sur (gate)'. The verb here is מסר 'to hand over/deliver' (post-biblical Hebrew), not סור. The ל prefix marks the infinitive construct 'to deliver/hand over'.
שמי: Candidates given are H8060 'Shammai' and H4310 'who'. Neither fits. This is שם 'name' (H8034) + 1cs suffix י = 'my name'.
textual_notes: וירדופ6כם contains a numeral '6' which appears to be a scribal mark or textual corruption. Reading as וירדפוכם 'and they will persecute you' from root רדף (H7291).
כנסיות has no Strong's candidates — this is a post-biblical Hebrew term for 'synagogues/assemblies' (plural of כנסיה/כנסת).
ובמשמרותם has no Strong's candidates — from משמרת/משמר 'guard/prison/watch' (related to H4929) with 3mp suffix, meaning 'their prisons' or 'their guard-posts'.
למסור: The Strong's candidates for סור don't match. This is the post-biblical Hebrew verb מסר 'to hand over/deliver up'.

verses.literal: Only before all these the things they will send against you their hands and will persecute you and will deliver you in houses of assemblies and in their prisons to deliver you to kings great for sake of my name

verses.translation: And this will come to you as [a] testimony [or: witness]

translation_notes: זה (consonants זה): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this'. Chose H2088 — 'and this will come to you for testimony' is coherent; 'a sheep will come' would be bizarre in context.

verses.literal: And this will come to you for testimony

verses.translation: Then let your heart be at rest [or: be settled], and do not think about in what manner [or: way] you will answer

translation_notes: ינוח (consonants י-נ-ו-ח): The only candidate listed is H3239, a place name 'Janoach.' However, the consonants נ-ו-ח clearly correspond to the root נוח (to rest, H5117), here in a jussive/imperfect form. With 'your heart' as subject, 'let [it] rest' is the only coherent reading. The place name makes no sense in context.

ואל (consonants א-ל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'strength/God', H413 'to/near'. Followed by תחשבו (you will think), the deprecative negation H408 fits perfectly: 'do not think.' A directive to God or a preposition would be incoherent here.

באי (consonants ב+א-י): Candidates: H335 'where?/how?', H336 'not', H337 'alas!', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Combined with זה ('this'), the phrase באי זה reads as 'in which' — an interrogative construction. H335 'where/how' best supports this reading as an indirect question about manner.

אופן (consonants א-ו-פ-ן): H212 'a wheel.' However, in later Hebrew אופן also means 'manner, way, mode' (derived from the wheel concept). Given the context 'in what ___ you will answer,' 'manner/way' is the coherent reading.
תענו: Root ע-נ-ה (to answer, H6030), 2mp imperfect. No Strong's candidate listed but the root is clear from context.
textual_notes: אופן H212 literally means 'wheel' but is used in post-biblical Hebrew for 'manner/way.' This text appears to use the later semantic development, suggesting a late or medieval Hebrew composition.
תענו could theoretically derive from ע-נ-ה 'to answer' (H6030) or ע-נ-ה 'to be afflicted' (H6031). Context strongly favors 'answer' since the passage discusses how to respond.

verses.literal: Then [let] rest your-heart and not think in-which this manner you-will-answer

verses.translation: For I will give to you power [or: strength, capacity] and wisdom, which [against it] your enemies will not be able to speak against [or: contradict]

translation_notes: אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. With 'will give to you' following, H589 'I' is the only coherent subject.

שאליה: This appears to be the relative particle ש + אליה ('that to-it/her'). The candidates listed for אליה are H451 'fat tail of sheep' and H452 'Elijah.' Neither fits. The consonants אל+יה read as the preposition אל with 3fs suffix ('to it/her'), referring back to the feminine noun חכמה (wisdom). The ש is a relative particle: 'which, to it.'
לאמר: Candidates include H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Context requires an infinitive of speaking: 'to say/speak against.' H559 is the clear choice.
נגדה: Root נגד with directional/suffix ה. Means 'against it/opposite it.' Refers to the wisdom given — enemies cannot speak against it.
textual_notes: שאליה is parsed as ש+אל+יה (relative particle + preposition 'to' + 3fs suffix). An alternative parsing as ש+אליה (that + Elijah or fat tail) is contextually impossible.
נגדה could be parsed as נגד+ה (against it, 3fs suffix referring to חכמה) or as a noun 'declaration.' The prepositional reading fits the syntax better.

verses.literal: For I will-give to-you power and-wisdom that-to-it not they-will-be-able to-say against-it your-enemies

verses.translation: And you will be handed over [or: delivered up, betrayed] by your fathers and by your brothers and by [your] kin and by [your] friends, and they will put to death some of you [with] death
words: and you will be handed over
and they will bring near/put forward

translation_notes: בעד: Candidates include H1157 'at, beside, behind, for, by' and various readings of עד. Here בעד is repeated four times introducing agents of betrayal (fathers, brothers, kin, friends). H1157 as 'by' (agent marker) fits: 'you will be handed over by your fathers.' This is more natural than 'for/on behalf of' since the subject is betrayal.
קצת: Candidates H7117/H7118 'a portion, some.' In context 'some of you' makes perfect sense with מכם following.
textual_notes: בעד could mean 'by' (agent of betrayal — you will be delivered by your family) or 'on account of' (delivered because of your family). The parallel structure with four family/social categories strongly suggests these are the agents doing the delivering/betraying.

וינגשו could derive from נגש 'to approach, drive' (H5065/H5066). If from H5065 (to oppress/exact), it could mean 'they will oppress'; if related to execution context, 'they will put forward [for death].' The following phrase 'some of you in death' suggests a judicial or violent action.
ותמסרו: root מסר (to hand over, deliver). The Niphal/passive form means 'you will be handed over/betrayed.'

verses.literal: And-you-will-be-handed-over by fathers-your and-by brothers-your and-by kin and-by friends and-they-will-put-to-death some from-you in-death

verses.translation: And you will be cursed [or: hated, despised] by all humanity on account of my name

translation_notes: אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be rosy', H120 'a human being/mankind', H121 'Adam (proper name)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby/garnet'. After מכל ('from all'), H120 'mankind' produces the coherent image 'cursed by all humanity.' H121 Adam or H123 Edom would narrow it to one person/nation, which is less fitting with 'all.'
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of, in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Context requires a causal conjunction: 'on account of my name.' H5668 is the clear choice.

שמי: Candidates listed: H8060 'Shammai' (proper name), and מי H4310 'who?'. However, the consonants שם+י naturally read as 'my name' (שם H8034 + 1cs suffix). Neither listed candidate fits as well as this straightforward possessive reading.
textual_notes: ארורים could be parsed as a passive participle of ארר (to curse, H779) — 'cursed ones' — or possibly from a root meaning 'hated/detested.' The standard reading 'cursed' fits the persecution context.
שמי: The listed candidates (Shammai, or ש+מי 'that who?') do not fit context. The natural reading is שם 'name' (H8034) with 1cs possessive suffix: 'my name.'

verses.literal: And-you-will-be cursed from-all mankind on-account-of my-name

verses.translation: And [not even] a single hair [or: strand] of your head will perish [or: be lost, be destroyed]

translation_notes: ושער: Candidates: H8175 'to storm/shiver', H8176 'to act as gatekeeper/estimate', H8177 'hair', H8178 'tempest/terror', H8179 'gate/door', H8180 'a measure'. With ראשכם ('your head') following, H8177 'hair' is the only reading that produces a coherent physical image: 'hair of your head.'

נימא: Not in the provided Strong's candidates. This appears to be a post-biblical Hebrew / Aramaic word נימא meaning 'thread, strand, hair.' It functions as a unit specifier for the 'one' — 'one strand.'
תפסד: No Strong's candidate provided. Root פסד appears to mean 'to cease, perish, be destroyed' — a post-biblical/Aramaic usage. 'Will not perish' completes the assurance.
textual_notes: נימא is not a standard biblical Hebrew word; it appears to be Aramaic/Mishnaic Hebrew for 'thread/strand/hair.' This confirms the text's late linguistic register.
תפסד likewise appears post-biblical. The root פסד in Aramaic/late Hebrew means 'to spoil, perish, be lost.' No biblical Strong's number applies directly.

verses.literal: And-hair [of] your-head one strand not will-perish

verses.translation: By your patient endurance [or: steadfast perseverance] you will gain [or: acquire, possess] your souls [or: your lives, your very selves]

translation_notes: בסבלנותכם: The root סבל means 'to bear/carry a burden' (H5445). The form סבלנות is an abstract noun meaning 'patience, endurance' — a post-biblical formation. With ב prefix and 2mp suffix: 'by your endurance.'
תנחלו: Root נחל (H5157) 'to inherit, take as possession.' 2mp imperfect: 'you will inherit/possess.'
נפשכם: נפש (H5315) 'soul, life, self' with 2mp suffix: 'your souls/lives.'
textual_notes: סבלנות is a post-biblical Hebrew abstract noun formation not found in the biblical lexicon. Its meaning 'patience/endurance' is well established in later Hebrew.
תנחלו could mean 'you will inherit' or 'you will gain/acquire.' Both are valid for נחל. The context of gaining one's soul through endurance slightly favors 'gain/acquire.'

verses.literal: In-your-endurance you-will-inherit your-souls

verses.translation: But when you see Jerusalem encircled [or: surrounded] by a great army [or: force], then know that the removal of her consolation [or: her desolation] has drawn near

translation_notes: רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. As an introductory particle to a conditional clause, H7535 'only/but' is the natural reading.

כאשר: The כ prefix + אשר. Candidates for אשר: H834 'who/which/when' is the relative/temporal conjunction. כאשר = 'when/as.' Other candidates (happiness, Asher, step) make no sense with the כ prefix in this temporal clause.

מחיל: Candidates: H2426 'army/intrenchment', H2427 'birth-throe', H2428 'force/army/wealth/strength', H2429 'army/strength'. With מ prefix ('from/by') and the image of Jerusalem surrounded, H2428 'army/force' fits: 'surrounded by a great army.' H2427 'birth-throe' would be incoherent.

סילוק: Not a biblical Hebrew word. Post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew from the root סלק 'to go up, depart, remove.' Means 'removal, departure.' Combined with נחמתה ('her consolation'), it reads 'the removal of her consolation' — i.e., Jerusalem's comfort being taken away.
נחמתה: Root נחם (H5162) 'to comfort/console' — noun נחמה 'consolation' with 3fs suffix: 'her consolation.'
textual_notes: סילוק is Mishnaic/post-biblical Hebrew, not found in Strong's. This word strongly marks the text as a late Hebrew composition.

נחמתה: 'her consolation' — the suffix refers to Jerusalem. An alternative reading could connect this to 'destruction' if one reads differently, but the consonants clearly support נחמה 'consolation' + ה suffix. The phrase 'removal of her consolation' = her desolation.
יראו appears to be 2mp ('you will see') based on context addressing 'you,' though the form could also be parsed as 3mp ('they will see'). The surrounding 2mp verbs (תדעו) suggest 2mp.

verses.literal: Only when you-will-see Jerusalem surrounded by-army great then you-will-know that-will-draw-near [the] removal [of] her-consolation

verses.translation: Then those who are in Judah, let them flee to the mountains; and those who are in her midst, let them depart [or: separate, withdraw]; and those who are in her surrounding regions, let them not enter into her

translation_notes: אשר (all three instances): Candidates include H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. As a relative pronoun introducing clauses ('those who are in Judah,' etc.), H834 is the only coherent reading.

הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham (region)', H1991 'abundance/wealth', H1992 'they (emphatic)'. In the clause 'and those who they [are] in her midst,' H1992 'they' serves as an emphatic pronoun — perfectly natural syntax.

אל: Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God/strength', H413 'to/near'. Before the jussive יכנסו ('let them enter'), H408 'not' creates the prohibition: 'let them not enter.' H413 'to' would be redundant with בה following.
textual_notes: באמצעה: ב + אמצע + ה. The noun אמצע ('middle, midst') is primarily post-biblical Hebrew. With 3fs suffix referring to Jerusalem: 'in her midst.'
יכנסו: root כנס (H3664 'to collect/gather'). In post-biblical Hebrew, כנס also means 'to enter.' The prohibition 'let them not enter into her' fits the flight-from-Jerusalem context.
בגבולותיה: גבול (H1366 'border, territory') with 3fs suffix and feminine plural: 'her borders/surrounding regions.'

verses.literal: Then [those] who will-be in-Judah let-them-flee to-the-mountains and-[those] who they [are] in-her-midst let-them-depart and-[those] who [are] in-her-borders not let-them-enter in-her

verses.translation: For these [are] the days — days of vengeance [or: retribution] they are — in order that all the things that were written will be fulfilled [or: completed]
words: in order that / on account of

translation_notes: אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak tree', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. However, אלה is also the common demonstrative pronoun 'these' (related to H428 אלה). In the phrase 'for these the days,' 'these' is the only coherent reading. None of the listed candidates fit.
נקם: Candidates: H5358 'to avenge/punish' (verb), H5359 'revenge/vengeance' (noun). Following יום ('day of'), a noun is required: H5359 'vengeance.' 'Days of vengeance.'
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. As a copular pronoun: 'they [are]' — H1992.
בעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of / in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Purpose clause: 'in order that all things written will be completed.' H5668.
textual_notes: אלה as 'these' (demonstrative pronoun) is not among the listed Strong's candidates, which all point to other roots. The demonstrative אלה is H428, not listed. The consonants are identical; I read it as the demonstrative.

שיושלמו: ש (relative) + יושלמו. Root שלם (H7999 'to be complete/finished'). The Pual or Huphal form: 'will be completed/fulfilled.' This could also be read as 'will be repaid' but 'fulfilled' fits the context of written prophecies being accomplished.
יום נקם: Could be construct ('day of vengeance') or apposition ('days — vengeance'). Construct is standard.

verses.literal: For these the-days days-of vengeance they [are] in-order-that will-be-completed all the-things that-were-written

verses.translation: And woe to those who will be pregnant and nursing in those days, for there will be great distress [or: oppression, anguish] upon the land and upon the people

translation_notes: ואוי: Candidates: H188 'lamentation/Oh!', H189 'Evi (proper name)'. As an interjection of distress ('woe!'), H188 is the clear choice.

הרות: The listed candidate is H7327 'Ruth (a Moabitess).' However, the consonants הרות clearly read as the feminine plural participle of הרה (H2030) 'pregnant.' With the ה prefix being part of the root: 'pregnant [women].' The proper name Ruth makes no sense.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/aloft', H5921 'upon/over/against', H5922 (Aramaic equivalent), H5923 'a yoke'. As a preposition before 'the land': H5921 'upon' is the standard reading.
והעם: Candidates: H5971 'a people/nation', H5972 (Aramaic), H5973 'with', H5974 (Aramaic 'with'). As a noun with the article and conjunction ('and the people'): H5971.
דוחק: Root דחק (H1849 related) 'to press, crowd, oppress.' The noun form means 'distress, pressure, oppression.' Post-biblical usage confirms this meaning.
לאותן: ל + אותן. Post-biblical Hebrew demonstrative/pronoun form: 'to those.' Not standard biblical Hebrew.
שתהיו: ש (relative) + תהיו (2fp or 3fp of היה). 'Who will be.' Refers to women who will be pregnant.
textual_notes: הרות: The consonants could theoretically be parsed as ה+רות (the + Ruth), but contextually 'pregnant women' (from root הרה) is overwhelmingly correct, especially paired with 'nursing.'

שתהיו: The form is ambiguous between 2nd person plural ('you who will be') and a late Hebrew 3rd person feminine plural. Given the 'woe to those' construction, 3fp ('who will be') is more natural, though the form looks 2mp.
Several words in this section (לאותן, באותן, דוחק, מיניקות) are characteristic of post-biblical/Mishnaic Hebrew, consistent with the linguistic register observed throughout this text.

verses.literal: And-woe to-those-who will-be pregnant and-nursing in-those the-days for will-be distress great upon the-land and-the-people

verses.translation: He will come until he strikes them by the edge [or: mouth] of the sword, and [they will be] led captive among all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled underfoot until the prophecy of the prophets is fulfilled [or: completed]

translation_notes: עד (first): Candidates: H5703 'terminus/duration', H5704 'until', H5706 'booty', H5707 'witness', H5708 'flux'. Chose H5704 because 'until' fits the temporal progression — he will come until he strikes them.
עד (second): Same candidates. Chose H5704 because 'until' introduces a temporal clause — Jerusalem trampled until the prophecy is completed.

ב3בי: The '3' appears to be a textual corruption or unusual character. From context (people being led away among nations), this likely represents שבי (captivity, H7628). The ב prefix gives 'in captivity'.
הסכין: H7915 'knife/blade'. In context with בפי ('by mouth of'), this is a weapon reference — 'by the edge of the blade/sword'.
textual_notes: ב3בי contains an unidentifiable character '3' — reconstructed as שבי (captivity) from context, but this is uncertain.
הסכין (knife) is unusual in military contexts where חרב (sword) is more common; 'the knife' or 'the blade' may be a variant translation tradition for a weapon's edge.
המכהו could be parsed as definite article + hiphil participle of נכה (H5221) with 3ms suffix ('the one striking him') or as a verbal form 'striking them'. Context suggests the latter.

verses.literal: He will come until striking-him by mouth of the knife and [they will be] brought in captivity among all the peoples and Jerusalem will be trampled until [the] prophecy of the prophets will be completed

verses.translation: And there will be seen signs [or: portents] in the sun and in the moon [or: the white one] and in the stars, and upon the earth distress among the peoples because of the confusion [or: tumult] of the roaring of the sea and its surging waves

translation_notes: ויראה: The candidates offer H3374 'fear/reverence'. However, the consonants ויראה equally support ו+יראה from ראה (H7200, 'to see'), niphal 'will be seen'. Given the subject 'אות' (signs), the reading 'will be seen' is far more coherent than 'fear'.
אות: H225 'to come/assent' vs H226 'a signal/sign'. Signs being seen in sun, moon, stars — H226 is the natural reading.

ובלבנה: Candidates: H3839 'whitish tree', H3840 'whiteness/transparency', H3841 'Libnah (place)', H3842 'the moon', H3843 'a brick'. Alongside sun and stars, H3842 'the moon' is the only coherent reading.
בעבור: H5668 'on account of, in order that' vs H5669 'stored grain'. The causal sense fits: distresses on account of tumults. Chose H5668.
ב3מש: The '3' is likely a textual corruption; from context (moon and stars alongside), this clearly refers to שמש (sun, H8121). The ב prefix gives 'in the sun'.
הים: H3220 'sea' vs H3222 'warm spring'. In context with waves/surf and cosmic signs, H3220 'the sea' is the obvious choice.
textual_notes: ב3מש contains an unidentifiable character '3' — reconstructed as שמש (sun) based on the celestial triad (sun, moon, stars).
ויראה could theoretically be parsed as וי+ראה (and he saw) or niphal ו+נראה (and was seen/appeared). The plural subject אות favors niphal 'will be seen' but could also be impersonal passive.

verses.literal: And will be seen signs in the sun and in the moon and in the stars and in the earth distresses to peoples on account of tumults [of] sound of the sea and its waves

verses.translation: People will be withered [or: dried up, faint] from fear and trembling [or: anxiety] that will come upon all the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken [or: will tremble]

translation_notes: וחרדה: H2731 'fear, anxiety' vs H2732 'Charadah (place)'. Paired with מיראה (from fear), H2731 'dread/anxiety' is the natural companion.
על: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/over/against', H5923 'a yoke'. Fear coming 'upon' the world — H5921 is the clear choice.
כל: H3605 vs H3606 (Aramaic equivalent). Standard Hebrew prose — H3605.
כי: H3587 'a brand/scar' vs H3588 'for/because'. Introducing a causal clause explaining why people are afraid — H3588.
ה<מים: The '<' is likely a textual corruption. Given the context of cosmic powers being shaken and the parallel with section 10, this represents שמים (heavens, H8064) with the definite article.
העולם: H5769 'time out of mind / eternity / world'. In context 'upon all the world' — the spatial sense of 'world' fits best.
textual_notes: ה<מים contains an unidentifiable character '<' — reconstructed as שמים (heavens) based on context (powers of the heavens being shaken is consistent with cosmic signs in section 2).
יבשים could be from יבש (H3001 'to dry up, wither') used metaphorically for fainting/losing vitality from fear, which is an unusual but vivid image.
כחות is the plural of כח (H3581 'strength, power'). 'Powers of the heavens' refers to the celestial forces.

verses.literal: The men will be dried-up from fear and dread that will come upon all the world for powers of the heavens will be shaken

verses.translation: Then they will see the Son of Humanity [or: Adam, mankind] coming in a cloud with a great, swift, dense [cloud-mass], and in the greatness of the image [or: figure, representation] of his likeness

translation_notes: בן: H1121 'a son' vs H1122 'Ben (personal name)' vs H1123 (Aramaic 'son'). In construct with האדם, H1121 'son' is the standard reading.

האדם: H119 'to flush/turn rosy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam (proper name)', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'redness/ruby'. With בן, 'son of the human' (H120) is the most coherent — a well-known prophetic title.
בענן: H6049 'to practice magic', H6050 (Aramaic 'cloud'), H6051 'a cloud', H6052 'Anan (name)'. Coming in a cloud with thick cloud — H6051 is the natural reading.
עם: H5971 'a people' vs H5973 'with (preposition)'. 'With a thick swift great [cloud]' — H5973 as preposition fits the syntax.
עב: H5645 'darkness/density/cloud' vs H5646 'architrave'. Alongside ענן (cloud), H5645 'thick cloud/density' is coherent.
קל: H7031 'light/rapid/swift' vs H7032 'voice/sound'. Describing the cloud — 'swift' (H7031) makes more sense than 'voice' alongside 'thick' and 'great'.

צלם: H6754 'phantom/illusion/resemblance/representative figure' vs H6755 'idolatrous figure'. In context of the Son of Humanity appearing in divine glory, H6754 'image/figure' fits better than 'idol'.
textual_notes: עב קל גדול — the relationship between these three adjectives and the noun is ambiguous. They could all modify ענן (cloud) or עב could be a separate noun ('a thick cloud, swift [and] great'). The phrase may describe one massive, swift, dense cloud-formation.

ובגודל צלם דמותו — 'in the greatness of the image of his likeness' is an unusual construct. This could mean 'in the magnitude of his visible form' or 'in a great representation of his appearance.' The layering of צלם and דמות together is reminiscent of Genesis 1:26.
קל could be H7032 'sound/voice' yielding 'with a thick [cloud], a great sound' — an alternate parsing that would parallel other theophany descriptions.

verses.literal: Then they will see [the] son of the human that will come in a cloud with a thick swift great [cloud] and in greatness of image of his likeness

verses.translation: And when these things [begin to happen], take notice [or: discern, observe] and lift up your heads and look, for your redemption [or: deliverance] is drawing near

translation_notes: וכאשר: The כ prefix + אשר. H834 'who/which/what/that/when' — as a temporal conjunction 'when' fits perfectly: 'and when these things...'

אלה: Candidates include H421 'bewail', H422 'adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, the consonants אלה also match the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (H428, often listed under אלה). In context 'these the things' — demonstrative pronoun is the only coherent reading.
ושאו: The candidates list H176 'or/if' for או, but ושאו is clearly ו+שאו from נשא (H5375 'to lift up'). The imperative 'lift up' paired with 'your heads' is coherent.
כי: H3587 'brand/scar' vs H3588 'for/because'. Introducing the reason to look up — H3588.
textual_notes: אלה is parsed as the demonstrative 'these' (H428) rather than any of the listed candidates (H421-H426), as none of those produce a coherent reading before הדברים.

תבוננו — hitpolel/hitpael of בין (H995), meaning 'discern/perceive/understand'. Could also be parsed as 'you will observe yourselves' but 'take notice/discern' fits the imperative tone of the passage.

verses.literal: And when these the things you will discern and lift [your] heads and look for your redemption [is] approaching

verses.translation: And he said to them: This [is] the illustration [or: form, pattern] — observe the fig tree and the rest of the trees

translation_notes: ואמר: H559 'to say' vs H560 (Aramaic 'to say') vs H561 'something said' vs H563 'a lamb' vs H564 'Immer (name)'. With ו prefix and followed by להם, H559 'and he said' is the clear choice.
להם: H3859 'to burn in/rankle' vs ל+הם H1992 'they/them'. 'And he said to them' — prepositional ל + pronoun הם (H1992) is the obvious reading.

התאנה: H8385 'an opportunity/purpose' is listed. However, the consonants תאנה also match H8384 (fig tree), which is unlisted but is the standard word. In context with 'trees' and agricultural imagery, 'fig tree' is the coherent reading.

ושאר: H7603 'yeast-cake', H7604 'to swell/be redundant', H7605 'a remainder', H7606 (Aramaic 'remainder'), H7607 'flesh/kindred'. Before האילנות (the trees), H7605 'the rest/remainder' is the only coherent choice.
textual_notes: התאנה: The listed candidate H8385 means 'opportunity/purpose', but the consonants are identical to H8384 'fig tree' (תאנה). Given the agricultural context and mention of trees, H8384 is almost certainly correct despite not being listed.
הצורה (H6699) — 'a form' or 'a rock'. In context, 'form/pattern/illustration' (a parable or analogy) makes more sense than 'rock'.

verses.literal: And he said to them this [is] the form see the fig-tree and [the] rest of the trees

verses.translation: When they produce [or: make] their fruits, you know that the summer [or: harvest season] is drawing near

translation_notes: אתם: The listed candidate H864 is 'Etham (place name)'. However, the consonants אתם are the standard second-person masculine plural pronoun 'you' (H859). In context 'you know' — the pronoun is the obvious reading.
שהקיץ: The ש prefix ('that') + ה definite article + קיץ H7019 'harvest/summer'. 'That the summer/harvest is approaching' fits the agricultural metaphor.
textual_notes: אתם: Listed candidate H864 (Etham, a place) does not fit; this is clearly the pronoun 'you' (H859), which shares the same consonants.

verses.literal: When making their fruits you know that the summer [is] approaching

verses.translation: So [or: likewise], when you see all these things come to pass [or: happen], you will know that the kingdom of YHWH [is] near

translation_notes: כן: H3651 'so/thus' vs H3652 (Aramaic 'so') vs H3653 'pedestal/stand' vs H3654 'gnat'. Introducing a comparison ('so, likewise') — H3651.
כאשר: H834 'when/that' vs others. Temporal conjunction 'when' — H834.
אלה: Same as section 5 — demonstrative 'these' (H428) before הדברים.

שיעשו: Listed candidate H3299 'Jaasu (name)'. However, the consonants ש+יעשו clearly represent the relative particle ש + imperfect of עשה (H6213 'to do/make'), niphal or qal: 'that will be done/happen'. The proper noun reading is contextually impossible.
יהוה: H3068 vs H3069 — both refer to the divine name. H3068 is standard.
textual_notes: שיעשו: The listed candidate H3299 (Jaasu) is a proper name that makes no sense here. This is ש + יעשו (qal/niphal imperfect 3mp of עשה H6213), meaning 'that will be done' or 'that will happen'.
אלה is again parsed as the demonstrative 'these' (H428) rather than any listed candidate.

verses.literal: So when you will see all these the things that will be done you will know that [the] kingdom of YHWH [is] near

verses.translation: In truth [or: faithfulness], I say to you that this generation will not pass away [or: die] until all these matters [or: affairs] come to pass

translation_notes: אני: H589 'I' vs H590 'a ship/fleet'. First person speaker — H589.
אומר: Listed candidate H201 'Omar (name)'. However, the consonants אומר are the qal active participle of אמר (H559 'to say'): 'saying/I say'. The proper noun reading is impossible in context.
שלא: ש (relative particle 'that') + לא H3808 'not'. Chose H3808 over H3809 (Aramaic equivalent) for standard Hebrew.
זה: H2088 'this' vs H2089 'a sheep' vs H2090 'this/that'. Before הדור ('the generation'), H2088 'this' is the clear reading.

הדור: H1752 'to gyrate/remain', H1753 'to reside', H1754 'circle/ball', H1755 'generation/age', H1756 'Dor (place)'. 'This the generation will not die' — H1755 'generation' is the only coherent reading.
עד: H5704 'until' — temporal clause 'until all these things are done'. Same reasoning as section 1.

שכל: The candidates list שכל as H7919-H7922 (intelligence/bereave) and כל as H3605. This is ש (that) + כל (H3605 'all'): 'that all'. The reading as a single word meaning 'intelligence' would break the sentence.
אלה: Demonstrative 'these' (H428) as in previous sections.
יעשו: Same as section 8 — H3299 'Jaasu' listed but clearly עשה H6213 imperfect 3mp: 'will be done'.
textual_notes: אומר: Listed as H201 (Omar, proper name) but is clearly the participle of אמר (H559). The candidate list appears incomplete.
שכל could theoretically be read as a single word H7919/H7922 ('understanding/intelligence'), but the syntax demands ש + כל ('that all').

העניינים — this appears to be a later Hebrew form (ענין, 'matter/affair', from Ecclesiastes usage) with plural suffix. Closest Strong's would be H6045 (ענין) though the form is characteristic of post-biblical Hebrew.

verses.literal: In truth I [am] saying to you that not will die this the generation until that all these the matters will be done

verses.translation: The heavens and the earth will come to an end [or: be consumed, perish], but my words will not pass away

translation_notes: ה<מים: Same as section 3 — the '<' is a textual corruption; this represents השמים (the heavens, H8064), paired with והארץ (and the earth).

ודברי: Listed candidate H1704 'Dibri (name)'. However, the consonants are clearly ו+דבר+י = 'and my words' (from דבר H1697 'word/thing' with 1cs possessive suffix). The proper noun reading makes no sense.
לא: H3808 vs H3809 (Aramaic). Standard Hebrew negation — H3808.
textual_notes: ה<מים contains the same unidentifiable '<' character as section 3. Reconstructed as שמים (heavens) based on the classic pair 'heavens and earth'.
ודברי: Listed only as H1704 (Dibri, proper name), but this is clearly ו + דברי ('and my words') from H1697 with first-person singular suffix.

verses.literal: The heavens and the earth will be finished and my words not will pass away

verses.translation: Guard yourselves lest your hearts become weighed down [or: burdened, dulled] with excess of food and drunkenness and the anxieties of this life, and that day come upon you suddenly

translation_notes: שבאולי (אולי): Candidates: H194 'perhaps/if not', H195 'Ulai river', H196 'foolish/impious'. The prefix ש functions as 'that/lest' and אולי as 'perhaps'; this creates 'lest perhaps' which fits the warning context perfectly.

כבד: Candidates: H3513 'to be heavy/burdensome', H3514 'weight/vehemence', H3515 'heavy/severe/dull', H3516 'liver'. Chose H3515 (adjective 'heavy/burdened') because it modifies לבבכם (your hearts) as a predicate adjective — hearts becoming heavy/dull from excess.
זה (first occurrence): Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 because 'this the life' is a demonstrative modifier, coherent in context.
וזה: Same candidates. Chose H2088 — 'and this the day' continues the parallel demonstrative structure.
textual_notes: ה<מרו contains an unidentified character '<'; the consonants suggest a reflexive imperative form of שמר (to guard/watch), read as הִשָּׁמְרוּ. The < may represent a scribal convention or damaged letter.

ובצורך could parse as ב + צורך 'in the need/anxiety of' or potentially relate to צור (distress/siege). The reading 'anxieties/cares' fits the context of life's burdens alongside gluttony and drunkenness.

verses.literal: Guard yourselves lest your hearts not be heavy in excess [of] eating and drunkenness and in [the] need [of] this the life and this the day comes suddenly upon you

verses.translation: And so [or: thus] it will come upon all [who] dwell [on the] face of the earth [or: ground, soil]

translation_notes: כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/upright', H3652 'so', H3653 'stand/pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 as the adverbial 'so/thus' — 'and so it will come' is the natural continuation of the preceding warning.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top/aloft', H5921 'upon/over/against', H5922 same, H5923 'yoke'. Chose H5921 'upon' because it governs the object 'all dwellers' — something coming upon people.

האדמה: Candidates: H126 'Admah (place)', H127 'soil/ground', H128 'Adamah (place)'. Chose H127 because 'face of the ground/earth' is a standard Hebrew expression for the surface of the earth, and the article ה suggests a common noun, not a proper noun.

verses.literal: And so it-comes upon all dwellers [of the] face [of] the ground

verses.translation: And therefore [or: on account of this] be awake at all times and pray to YHWH that you be found worthy to escape [or: flee from] all these things that are destined to come, standing [before the] Son of Man [or: the human one]

translation_notes: זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — 'and upon this' = 'therefore/on account of this', referring back to the preceding warning.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak/strong tree', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. None of these fit. The word אלה here functions as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (typically catalogued under H428 אֵלֶּה). The candidates listed share the consonants but the demonstrative pronoun is the only coherent reading before הדברים 'the things'.

לברוח: The candidates given are for רוח: H7304 'to breathe freely/revive', H7305 'room/deliverance', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 same. However, the ל + ברוח more naturally reads as the infinitive of ברח (to flee, H1272) — לברוח 'to flee'. The context of escaping calamities strongly supports 'to flee/escape' rather than any reading from רוח.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'a son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'a son'. Chose H1121 — 'son of the man' is a title/designation.

האדם: Candidates: H119 'to be red', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'son of the man/human' is a known title, and the article ה points to the generic 'the human' rather than the proper name Adam.
textual_notes: The placement of עומד (standing) is syntactically ambiguous: it could describe the subject who stands before the Son of Man (i.e., 'to stand before the Son of Man'), or it could begin a new clause ('the Son of Man stands'). The former reading — that the faithful will be found standing before the Son of Man — fits the preceding infinitive chain (worthy to flee... [and to] stand).
לעולם could mean 'forever' (H5769) or 'at all times' — both are valid for the same consonants. The context of watchfulness suggests 'at all times' is the primary sense.

אלה as 'these' (demonstrative) does not match any of the provided Strong's candidates, which all share the consonants אלה but have different meanings. The demonstrative pronoun אלה is typically H428. I assign it as such despite it not being in the candidate list.

verses.literal: And upon this wake-up for-ever and pray to YHWH that-you-be worthy to-flee all these the-things that-are-destined to-come standing [before the] son [of] the-man

verses.translation: During the day [he was] teaching in the sanctuary [or: temple] this generation [or: in that splendid manner]

translation_notes: מלמד: Candidates: H4451 'a goad for oxen', H3925 'to teach (by goading)', H4055 'measure/garment'. Chose H3925 — the form מלמד is a piel participle of למד 'to teach', meaning 'teaching/was teaching'. A goad (H4451) makes no sense in context of someone acting in a sanctuary.

במקדש: Candidates: H4720 'sanctuary/consecrated place', H6942 'to be clean/holy', H6943 'Kedesh', H6944 'a sacred place', H6945 'devotee', H6946 'Kadesh'. Chose H4720 because the prefix ב + מקדש = 'in the sanctuary/temple', which is the expected noun form.
textual_notes: זההדור appears to be a compound or run-together of זה + הדור. הדור could be from דור (H1755 'generation/age') or הדור meaning 'splendor/majesty' (H1926). Reading as 'this generation' fits a narrative context, but 'the splendid/glorious [one]' is also possible. I read it as 'this the generation' based on the demonstrative + noun pattern seen elsewhere in this text.
The section appears fragmentary — it may be a temporal clause ('During the day he was teaching in the temple...') that introduces the following narrative.

verses.literal: In-the-day [he was] teaching in-the-sanctuary this-the-generation

verses.translation: And all the people rose in the morning and came to the temple in order that they might hear him. [...] And they said, Lord, behold, two knives [are] here. And he said to them, [It is] enough.

translation_notes: העם: Candidates: H5971 'a people', H5973 'with (preposition)'. Chose H5971 because 'all the people rose' requires a noun subject.
במקדש: Candidates: H4720 'sanctuary/temple', H6942-H6946 (various). Chose H4720 because 'in the temple' is the most natural reading with the ב prefix.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 because the exclamatory 'behold' introduces a presentation of objects — 'behold, two knives here'.
שתי: Candidates: H8358 'intoxication', H8359 'warp in weaving'. Neither fits; שתי is the construct form of שתים 'two' (feminine). This is the numeral 'two' modifying סכינים.
פה: Candidates: H6310 'mouth', H6311 'here'. Chose H6311 because 'two knives here' describes location of the items being shown.
והוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun subject of 'said'.
די: Candidates: H1767 'enough', H1768 'that (relative)'. Chose H1767 because 'enough' is the response to being shown two knives.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/master/lord', H114 'Addon'. Chose H113 as a title of address.
textual_notes: The text has damaged/missing portions indicated by ] [ and diacritical marks (!, ״). The section appears to conflate two different narrative moments — the people coming to the temple to hear him (morning scene) and the disciples showing knives (evening/supper scene). There may be a lacuna or editorial join.
שתי: The Strong's candidates (intoxication, warp) do not match the numeral 'two', which is the obvious reading. This is the feminine construct numeral שתי from שתים.
בבק!ר: The ! likely indicates textual damage or uncertainty in the manuscript at this point. Reading as בבקר 'in the morning'.

verses.literal: And-all the-people rose in-the-morning and-came in-the-temple in-order-that they-would-hear-him [...] And-they said lord behold two knives here and-he said to-them enough
